item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"ARC-AGI-2 supports comparisons of success on unfamiliar grid problems under specified evaluation conditions. Its example-based tasks, separation of development and evaluation sets, and checks for repeated rules support that purpose. Human solving data informed selection, but the study included a larger pool than the final benchmark, and matching human difficulty does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI systems. Exact grid matching gives a clear correctness criterion, while averaging input success within problems means scores must be distinguished from counts of fully solved problems. Verified settings and spending limits help comparisons, but single-run evaluation and missing estimates of repeat variation limit interpretation of small differences. Public exposure, corrections and differing evaluation routes also require attention when comparing results. The supplied evidence supports a bounded measure of grid-task performance; broader reasoning and intelligence claims remain unresolved.","supported_claims":["The tasks require inferring a rule from example grids and producing exact outputs, directly supporting evaluation of performance on this task format.","Development and evaluation sets are separate, and human solving results informed selection of test sets with similar human difficulty.","Public problems, scoring software, marking tests and dated corrections support inspection of task content and scoring procedures.","Verified evaluations specify settings and spending limits, providing a defined basis for comparisons within those conditions."],"documented_problems":["Public evaluation problems are accessible, creating an exposure concern; hidden-test safeguards also acknowledge possible leakage.","Corrections to squares and unclear examples show that released materials required revision, and affected AI scores are not all recalculated.","Verified testing uses one run, leaving reported results without averaging across repeated runs.","A nearly correct grid receives no credit, so scores omit partial progress within an output grid."],"missing_information":["Repeated-run score variation and systematic effects of instructions, presentation and software changes are not supplied.","The inspected marking tests do not establish independent verification of the entire scoring system.","The supplied studies do not establish prediction of performance in language, social interaction or real-world work.","The complete archive of reported outputs, costs, times and problem scores was not checked."],"reinterpretations":["Interpret a score as an average of within-problem input success under two permitted attempts, rather than the percentage of problems fully solved.","Similar human difficulty across test sets does not establish equivalent AI difficulty or AI score stability.","Resistance to program search and repeated-rule checks support the intended design but do not prove that high scores require the intended reasoning.","Compare results with their evaluation route, settings, spending limit and revision identified; ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions."],"closing_note":"Reporting should clarify whether “solved” means an exact input answer or every input in a problem, and identify the applicable evaluation rules and version."},{"benchmark":"designqa","instrument_review":"DesignQA provides a practically grounded assessment of finding and applying rules and interpreting vehicle materials within Formula SAE. Its six task groups cover several relevant activities, but one rulebook, uneven group sizes and limited review evidence constrain coverage and confidence in the answer keys. Scoring mixes text similarity with decision accuracy, and documented wording effects mean credit can reflect expression as well as engineering understanding. Equal weighting of groups defines an overall summary without establishing a single underlying competence. Comparisons also depend on information supply: whole-rulebook and retrieved-passage conditions evaluate different system configurations. Limited variation evidence, very small groups and incomplete historical records weaken fine rankings and reproducibility. The scores are informative about these tasks under stated conditions, while transfer to other documents or engineering projects remains unestablished.","supported_claims":["Real competition rules, vehicle designs and test data give the questions a concrete connection to engineering activities.","The six groups examine rule finding, terminology, component recognition, dimensions and performance requirements.","Additional reviewers checked manually written questions with stated exceptions, providing some quality control.","Public questions, instructions, scoring code and some responses allow partial inspection, and experiments examine sensitivity to supplied materials."],"documented_problems":["Coverage is concentrated: individual-rule finding has 1,192 questions, while functional performance has only 16.","Scoring examples show sensitivity to commas and omission of valid related rules from supplied answers.","Systems receive different information supplies, so reported differences cannot be attributed solely to the AI models.","All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes strategy to earn decision credit on that portion; use of that strategy by tested systems is not established.","Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to each result, and one answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding reported question count."],"missing_information":["Reviewer disagreement rates and remaining answer errors are not established, and some explanations received only limited checks.","Complete evidence of marking accuracy and consistency, and evidence that group or overall scores measure distinct skills, are absent.","Identical-condition repeat variation is not isolated; changing passage sets does not provide that estimate.","No human-engineer baseline, established protected test set, systematic overlap check or sufficiently clear training and repeated-submission rules are supplied.","A clear record of revision effects, a licence file and complete reuse rules were not found in the inspected materials; this does not establish that reuse is prohibited."],"reinterpretations":["Interpret results as performance of an AI together with its supplied documents or retrieval system.","Treat the overall score as an equally weighted summary of six differently sized and scored groups, rather than accuracy across all questions or established general engineering competence.","Treat close rankings cautiously: one additional correct answer changes performance-group accuracy by 6.25 percentage points.","Correct yes/no decisions and text-similarity scores provide different evidence; neither alone establishes sound engineering explanations.","Practical source materials establish relevance, while success on other technical documents and real projects remains uncertain."],"closing_note":"Instructions and reports should specify acceptable alternative answers, formatting requirements, information supplied to each system and the exact scoring revision used."}]}
